A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SINGAPO work, with matching main sections, quantitative experiments and original appendices. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; v3 extends Appendix A.5.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, component and data-augmentation ablations, and a 48-participant user study in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative demonstrations of real-image reconstruction, interactive editing and testing on articulated-state inputs.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o graph prediction, DINOv2 conditioning, diffusion architecture, training losses and mesh retrieval remain unchanged. The added editing demonstrations elaborate the pipeline's previously claimed editability without documenting an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds zero-shot testing on PartNet-Mobility objects shown in randomized articulated states and interactive scenarios with user-edited graphs. The existing datasets remain unchanged. Real internet-image testing was already reported in v1, so Figure 10 does not establish an entirely new domain.

E2.justification: URDFormer, NAP-ICA and their oracle variants retain the same participation in the corresponding comparisons. The Real2Code comparison is also unchanged, and the added qualitative demonstrations introduce no comparators.

E3.justification: The new Appendix A.5 evaluations randomize test-object articulation and viewpoints without retraining, and demonstrate interventions through graph correction, graph editing and part-label specification. Existing splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged; the explicit resting-state training description is a clarification.

E4.justification: Figures 11–12 add qualitative case studies of user intervention and robustness to non-resting inputs, including extreme-state failures. Existing component and augmentation ablations in Tables 4–5, and the earlier failure and metric analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Five-output averaging and references to different generation seeds remain unchanged in the existing experiments. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and the user-study mean rankings of 1.20, 1.91 and 2.89 are unchanged. Figures 10–12 add qualitative outputs illustrating real-image reconstruction, responses to editing, and successes and failures under articulated-state inputs.

T1.justification: The mathematical representations, losses and Hungarian-matched evaluation-metric definition remain unchanged. Correcting the motion-range symbol from t_i to r_i in Section 3.2 fixes notation without changing the underlying definition; no substantive theoretical additions appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about single-image articulated-object generation, the modular editable pipeline, and reconstruction quality and generalization. The new appendix demonstrations support existing claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 newly attributes failures under extreme articulation to self-occlusion, unfamiliar spatial structures and distracting exposed interiors, and states that outputs do not reproduce the input's articulation state. These extend v1's limitations concerning textures, small parts, clutter and geometric detail.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly identifies training renders as resting-state images, and Appendix A.5 describes randomized states and viewpoints for the new zero-shot test. These refine documented data preparation; implementation hyperparameters, hardware, GPT-4o prompt, retrieval details and the project-link destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the related-work discussion retains the same positioning relative to CAGE, NAP, URDFormer, Real2Code and other research. The small wording edits do not alter novelty claims or relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, revises the foreground-loss explanation, and expands Appendix A.5 with short discussions of the added demonstrations. The main section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds three supplementary multi-panel figures: real-image examples, interactive editing and articulated-state testing. Existing displays are retained, with small label changes in Figures 1 and 6, adjusted placement around Tables 8–9, and added conference headers.

improvement.justification: Figures 10–11 make the evidence for real-image applicability and editability more directly inspectable, while Figure 12 and its discussion clarify practical failure boundaries beyond resting-state inputs. These improve empirical transparency and interpretation. The additions remain qualitative, with no expanded quantitative or uncertainty evaluation, so the overall gain is limited.
